trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport around 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a leisurely walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — spot the exteriors of Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera for free from the street. Marvel at Gaudí's iconic architecture without paying entrance fees.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the nearby Rambla de Catalunya for a relaxed evening atmosphere. Explore the Eixample neighborhood streets and get oriented. Head to Plaça de Catalunya as the sun sets for a lively local scene.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — arrival day
meals.lunch: Pick up a bocadillo (sandwich) or slice of pizza from a local bakery or supermarket near the hotel for €3–5 to save money on arrival day
meals.dinner: Bar Calders (Carrer del Parlament) — a beloved local tapas bar in nearby Sant Antoni with affordable pintxos and tapas from €1.50–3 each. Budget around €12–15 total

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is hot (28–33°C). Pack light, stay hydrated, and carry a reusable water bottle. Public fountains across the city provide free drinking water. Validate your Metro T-Casual 10-trip card (€11.35) upon arrival — it will save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start early (8:00–9:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Walk to the iconic Sagrada Família (10-min walk from Eixample). Book tickets online in advance (€26 basic entry, or €36 with tower access) — this is the one must-spend splurge of the trip. Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, studying the intricate facades and soaring interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Sagrada Família, walk north to Park Güell (free access to most of the park; the Monumental Zone costs €10 but the surrounding terraces and views are free). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and panoramic views of the city. Take Metro L3 back toward the city center and visit the Palau de la Música Catalana exterior for free (interior tours cost extra — admire the stunning Modernista facade at no cost).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the El Born neighborhood for the evening. Explore the narrow medieval streets and browse the boutiques. Visit the Santa Maria del Mar church (free or small donation) — a stunning Gothic masterpiece. As night falls, join the locals at one of the many affordable bars in El Born for pre-dinner drinks.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Josep or any local bakery near the hotel — coffee and pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) for €3–4
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) near Sagrada Família — 3 courses including bread and a drink for €12–14. Look for handwritten chalkboard signs outside restaurants
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet (Carrer de Montcada, El Born) — a legendary cava bar serving affordable tapas and house cava. Budget €15–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance online to avoid sellouts and skip the queue. Wear comfortable shoes — expect 6–8 km of walking today. The Metro T-Casual card covers all transit.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro L3 to Barceloneta or walk down La Rambla (30 min) to reach the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic). Spend the morning exploring the labyrinthine medieval streets for free. Visit the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 PM), the Roman ruins of Barcino (visible through glass panels in the street for free), and Plaça Reial — a beautiful neoclassical square with Gaudí-designed lamp posts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through La Barceloneta to the beach for a couple of hours of free relaxation and swimming in the Mediterranean. Then head to the Barceloneta neighborhood to explore the waterfront. Walk along the Port Olímpic boardwalk and admire Frank Gehry's famous gold 'Fish' sculpture for free. Take the Metro or bus back toward Montjuïc and visit the Fundació Joan Miró exterior and surroundings (entry is €14 — skip inside if budget is tight, the outdoor sculptures are partially visible). Walk up to Mirador del Migdia for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample area. Explore the Gaixample (LGBTQ+ neighborhood within Eixample) for vibrant nightlife. Visit the rooftop bar at La Pepita or a similar affordable rooftop spot for sunset drinks. The Eixample nightlife scene heats up after 10 PM — bar hop along Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner for affordable cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia area in the Gothic Quarter — grab a coffee and tostada for €3–4 at any corner café
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada or a chiringuito (beach bar) in Barceloneta — try a classic bombas (potato croquette) for €2–3 each. Budget €10–12
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana (Carrer de Mallorca, Eixample) — popular tapas spot with excellent patatas bravas, croquetas, and montaditos. Budget €15–18. Arrive early (7 PM) to avoid the wait

day_by_day.notes: Barcelona beaches are free but can be very crowded in August. Keep valuables secured — pickpocketing is common in La Rambla and Gothic Quarter. Bars in Barcelona typically don't fill up until midnight; nightlife runs until 3–5 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro L3 to Diagonal or walk from the hotel to visit Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — choose one to enter as both are pricey (€25–35 each). La Pedrera rooftop is particularly spectacular and worth the splurge. Book online for discounts. Spend 1.5–2 hours inside. Alternatively, save money by admiring both exteriors on Passeig de Gràcia and spending the entry fee on food and nightlife instead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Bus 55 or Metro to Montjuïc. Ride the Montjuïc Cable Car (€12.70 return) or hike up for free. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry, free on Sundays) for sweeping views over the city and port. Explore the Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic terraces (€3.50 entry) — beautifully landscaped with Mediterranean plants. Descend via the Montjuïc Funicular (covered by Metro T-Casual card).
day_by_day.evening: This is your big nightlife night. Start with dinner in the El Raval neighborhood — edgy, multicultural, and affordable. After dinner, head to Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz (two of Barcelona's most famous clubs) — entry typically €12–18, often with one drink included. Alternatively, explore the free street parties and outdoor bars around Plaça del Sol in Gràcia neighborhood for a more local, low-cost experience. Clubs don't fill up until 1–2 AM.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café (Carrer del Parlament) — popular brunch spot with avocado toast and specialty coffee for €8–10 total
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni (near El Raval) — browse the market stalls for fresh fruit, olives, cheese, and local snacks. Assemble a picnic for €6–8
meals.dinner: Bar Marsella or nearby spots in El Raval — try a menú del día or tapas. Budget €12–15. Eat late (9–10 PM) like the locals

day_by_day.notes: If you plan to club, pre-buy tickets online to save on entry and sometimes get drink discounts. Wear comfortable shoes for dancing. Keep your group together and be aware of surroundings in busy nightlife areas. Last Metro runs around 12 AM on weekdays — after that, take night buses (Nitbus) or a taxi/rideshare.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved sleep-in (given the late night), wake up and enjoy a slow final morning in Barcelona. Walk to the Mercat de Sant Josep de la Boqueria on La Rambla (free to enter — buy a fresh juice for €1.50 and browse the stalls). Pick up any last-minute affordable souvenirs — olive oil, paprika, or local sweets from the market are better value than tourist shops. Take a final walk along Passeig de Gràcia to photograph the Modernista architecture in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout 11–12 PM — store luggage at the hotel if your flight is later). Visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art Barcelona) — even if not entering, the plaza outside is a famous skate spot and great for people-watching. Walk through El Raval one last time. Head to the airport via Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya (€5.90, runs every 5–10 minutes, takes 35 minutes) — allow 2–2.5 hours before departure.

meals.breakfast: La Boqueria market fresh juice (€1.50) + pan con tomate from a nearby café (€3–4) — a perfect final Barcelona breakfast
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable: grab a bocadillo from Conesa Entrepans in the Gothic Quarter (€4–6) or a slice of pizza from a local spot before heading to the airport

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget breakdown for 5 days (excluding flights and accommodation): Transport (Metro T-Casual + Aerobus x2): ~€25 | Sagrada Família: €26 | Park Güell Monumental Zone: €10 | La Pedrera or Casa Batlló: €25–35 | Castell de Montjuïc: €5 | Meals (avg €15–20/day): €75–100 | Nightlife (1 club night): €15–20 | Misc/souvenirs: €15–20. TOTAL ESTIMATE: €195–240 for 5 days in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via Aerobus or taxi (~35 min). Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll the iconic Passeig de Gràcia just steps from your hotel. Admire the exterior of the 'Block of Discord' — Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera — for a free introduction to Eixample's Modernisme architecture. Pick up a local SIM card or map if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona's nightlife with the Eixample Modernisme Bar Crawl along Carrer del Consell de Cent and surrounding streets. Start around 20:00 and explore the vibrant Gayxample bar scene and classic cocktail bars at a relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or a café near the hotel on arrival.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample spot for tapas and montaditos at mid-range prices (€15–20 per person). Arrive by 14:30 to beat the post-lunch rush.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda — a cozy, affordable wine bar and restaurant in Eixample offering Catalan classics like pa amb tomàquet and grilled meats (€20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00, so Day 1 is intentionally light. No pre-booked tours needed today. Book timed-entry tickets for Sagrada Família and Park Güell online tonight for later in the week — they sell out fast in August.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — book the 09:00 or 10:00 skip-the-line guided slot. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's iconic basilica with a knowledgeable guide covering the Nativity and Passion facades, the nave, and the towers. Arrive 15 minutes early.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Eixample and explore the Fundació Antoni Tàpies (€12 entry) on Carrer d'Aragó — a converted Moderniste publishing house showcasing contemporary Catalan art. Afterward, browse the upscale boutiques and architecture along Passeig de Gràcia at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert — attend a live performance at this breathtaking UNESCO-listed Moderniste hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Check the August program in advance and book tickets (€25–55 depending on performance). Dress smart-casual.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in Eixample — popular brunch spot with excellent coffee, avocado toast, and pastries (€10–14 per person). Arrive by 08:15 before your tour.
meals.lunch: Bar Calders in Sant Antoni (15-min walk from Sagrada Família) — relaxed terrace bar with excellent vermouth, pintxos, and daily specials (€12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Parking Pizza on Londres street — creative Neapolitan-style pizzas in a stylish Eixample setting (€18–24 per person). Time it for 19:30 to reach the concert comfortably.

day_by_day.notes: Sagrada Família is extremely busy in August — a skip-the-line guided tour is essential. The Palau de la Música is a 20-minute taxi or metro ride from Eixample (L4 to Urquinaona). Check the concert schedule at palaumusica.cat and book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — arrive at the monumental zone for your timed-entry slot (book 09:00 or 10:00 to beat the heat and crowds). Explore Gaudí's colorful mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the viaducts. Allow 1.5 hours inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood for a self-guided wander through its bohemian squares — Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, and Plaça de la Virreina. Browse independent boutiques, vintage shops, and local bookstores. Head back to Eixample for a mid-afternoon rest during peak heat (14:00–17:00).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the El Raval and Sant Antoni areas on foot — visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) exterior plaza, a hub of local street culture, then settle into the lively Sant Antoni market area for drinks at one of the many terrace bars that come alive after 20:00.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) at a local bar in Gràcia near Park Güell, such as Bar Canigó on Carrer de Verdi (€6–9 per person).
meals.lunch: La Pepita in Gràcia — celebrated for creative montaditos and fresh ingredients in a beautiful tiled space (€15–22 per person). Expect a short queue; arrive at 13:30.
meals.dinner: Bodega Cañete in El Raval — a lively, upscale tapas bar with excellent Catalan charcuterie, cheeses, and seasonal dishes (€25–35 per person). Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed tickets must be booked at parkguell.barcelona. The monumental zone tickets cost €10. August mornings heat up quickly — wear sunscreen and bring water. The park is a 20-minute taxi ride or bus (Bus 24 or V17) from Eixample.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — join a small-group guided walking tour (or follow a self-guided route) starting at the Plaça Nova and the Barcelona Cathedral. Wind through the atmospheric medieval lanes of the Barri Gòtic, discovering Roman ruins, hidden courtyards, and the Pont del Bisbe bridge. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross into El Born neighborhood and visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar — a stunning 14th-century Gothic church with a beautifully austere interior (free entry). Browse the boutiques and galleries of Carrer del Rec and Passeig del Born. Stop at the El Born Cultural Centre to see the excavated medieval ruins beneath the market (€6 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for a second, deeper dive into the Eixample Modernisme Bar Crawl — this time explore the cocktail bars and rooftop terraces you may have missed on Day 1. Try Dry Martini Bar (a Barcelona institution) and finish the night at one of the late-night clubs on Carrer de Muntaner or Carrer de Balmes.

meals.breakfast: Alsur Café in El Born — artisan coffee, fresh juices, and eggs Benedict in a relaxed setting (€12–16 per person). Walk or take the metro (L4 Jaume I) from Eixample.
meals.lunch: El Xampanyet in El Born — a legendary cava bar serving anchovies, conserves, and house cava in a timeless tiled space (€15–20 per person). Arrive early as it fills quickly.
meals.dinner: Bormuth on Carrer del Rec — a stylish El Born vermouth bar and restaurant with excellent tapas and natural wines (€20–28 per person). Great for a relaxed pre-nightlife dinner.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter tour is best done on foot — wear comfortable shoes as the cobblestones are uneven. Many Gothic Quarter small-group tours depart from Plaça de Catalunya (€15–25 per person). El Born is a 30-minute walk or short metro ride from Eixample (L4 Barceloneta or Jaume I).

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning in Eixample — visit the Mercat de l'Abaceria or browse the Sunday-style antique stalls at Mercat de Sant Antoni (open daily, major market on Sundays but open on weekdays for fresh produce). Pick up local ceramics, olive oil, or textiles as souvenirs. Enjoy a slow café breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Revisit your favorite Eixample Modernisme highlights at your own pace — consider booking a Casa Batlló interior visit (€35–40, book online) if you haven't already, or simply enjoy a final walk along Passeig de Gràcia. Pack and prepare for departure if flying out soon, or enjoy a leisurely swim at Barceloneta Beach (30-min metro ride, L4 Barceloneta).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample to cap the trip. Reflect on the week's highlights over a proper Catalan meal — finish with a walk along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia to admire the Moderniste lamp posts and facades one last time.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume on Rambla de Catalunya — a classic Barcelona pastry shop and café serving ensaïmades, croissants, and coffee (€8–12 per person). A perfect slow morning treat.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana for a return visit, or try Lateral on Passeig de Gràcia for a polished tapas lunch with excellent patatas bravas and jamón (€18–25 per person).
meals.dinner: Moments or a splurge at Disfrutar (book well in advance — Michelin-starred) if budget allows, OR a mid-range farewell at Restaurant Embat on Carrer de Muntaner — seasonal Catalan market cuisine in a warm, intimate setting (€30–40 per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: If departing on Day 5 evening or Day 6, keep the afternoon flexible for packing and airport transfer. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya takes 35 minutes to the airport and costs €6.75. Tip: Barcelona's August evenings are warm and lively — a final stroll along Passeig de Gràcia after dinner is free and magical.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Bodega Sepúlveda — a refined Eixample bistro serving elevated Catalan tapas and natural wines, perfect for a relaxed first afternoon meal.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar — two-Michelin-starred avant-garde restaurant in Eixample offering a theatrical tasting menu. Book well in advance. Ideal celebratory first-night dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Disfrutar tasting menu months ahead — it is one of the world's most sought-after reservations. Request a late seating (21:00–21:30) to align with Barcelona dining culture. Keep the afternoon light given travel fatigue.

day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for a sophisticated evening. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at Dry Martini Barcelona, a legendary upscale cocktail bar on Carrer d'Aribau. Follow with dinner at a nearby fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or Forn de Sant Jaume on Rambla de Catalunya — a beloved Eixample bakery-café with exceptional pastries and coffee.
meals.lunch: La Pepita — a stylish, design-forward restaurant in Gràcia known for creative montaditos and Catalan cuisine using seasonal market ingredients.
meals.dinner: Lasarte — three-Michelin-starred restaurant helmed by Martín Berasategui, located steps from Passeig de Gràcia. Expect exquisite Basque-Catalan haute cuisine and impeccable service.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book both Sagrada Família (private guided tour with tower access) and Park Güell monumental zone tickets online — both sell out weeks in advance in August. Wear comfortable shoes for Park Güell's uneven terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — join a premium small-group or private guided walking tour through the labyrinthine medieval Gothic Quarter. Highlights include the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Temple d'August Roman columns, and the Pont del Bisbe bridge. Transition into the adjacent El Born neighborhood to admire its elegant iron-and-glass Mercat de Santa Caterina and the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore El Born at your own pace — visit the El Born Cultural Centre (built over medieval ruins), browse high-end concept stores, and relax at a terrace café. Optional: private visit to the Museu Picasso with skip-the-line access.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert — attend a live performance at this breathtaking UNESCO-listed Art Nouveau masterpiece. Choose a classical, flamenco, or jazz program. Arrive early to admire the stained-glass ceiling and ornate interior before the show begins.

meals.breakfast: Nomad Coffee Lab & Shop in El Born — one of Barcelona's finest specialty coffee roasters, paired with artisan pastries.
meals.lunch: El Xampanyet — an iconic El Born cava bar and tapas institution. Order the house cava, anchovies, and patatas bravas in a convivial, authentic atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Besta — a celebrated contemporary Galician seafood restaurant in El Born with a refined tasting menu. Outstanding raw bar and natural wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música Catalana concert tickets well in advance — August programs sell out quickly. Opt for a premium seat in the central stalls for the best sightlines of the extraordinary interior. Smart casual attire is appropriate.

day_by_day.morning: Deep-dive architecture day: take a private guided tour of Casa Batlló (Gaudí) with the premium 'Magic Nights' or standard morning experience — the immersive audiovisual journey through the building is extraordinary. Afterward, walk to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for a rooftop visit, best appreciated in the morning light before crowds peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure and luxury recovery afternoon. Return to the hotel for a spa session or pool time if available. Alternatively, explore the upscale boutiques along Passeig de Gràcia and Carrer de Provença — browse Loewe, Custo Barcelona, and local Catalan design houses. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies, a modernist townhouse converted into a world-class contemporary art museum.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's elite nightlife scene. Begin with sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Mandarin Oriental or Hotel Arts for sweeping city views. Then head to a premium nightclub — Pacha Barcelona or Opium — for a late-night session with world-class DJs. Barcelona nightlife starts late; plan to arrive at clubs after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in Sant Antoni — a beloved Eixample brunch institution with excellent eggs, avocado toast, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Parking Pizza — deceptively named, this is a sophisticated Eixample restaurant with exceptional Neapolitan-style pizzas, natural wines, and a buzzy, design-led interior.
meals.dinner: Moments — two-Michelin-starred restaurant inside the Mandarin Oriental hotel, led by Carme Ruscalleda's team. Refined Catalan haute cuisine in an elegant setting.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Casa Batlló tickets online — the premium immersive experience sells out. For the nightclub, consider a table reservation or guestlist entry through the hotel concierge to avoid queues and ensure priority access. Dress code is smart-chic.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle final morning — enjoy a slow breakfast and pack. Take a last walk along Rambla de Catalunya or through the peaceful interior courtyards (illes) of Eixample. Visit Mercat de l'Abaceria or Mercat de Sant Antoni for a final taste of local market culture and pick up premium Catalan food souvenirs: artisan olive oil, aged cheeses, craft vermouth, and chocolate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Depending on departure time, enjoy a final leisurely lunch before transferring to Barcelona El Prat Airport (BCN). Allow at least 90 minutes for the airport transfer and check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of Barcelona's extraordinary architecture, cuisine, and nightlife home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Caravelle — a stylish Eixample café known for its excellent brunch, sourdough toasts, and specialty coffee roasts.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample classic serving outstanding pintxos, fresh seafood, and cold cava in a relaxed, buzzy atmosphere. Perfect final Barcelona meal.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport — Terminal 1 at BCN has a good selection of dining options for a final Catalan bite before departure.

day_by_day.notes: Ask the hotel concierge to arrange a premium private transfer to Barcelona El Prat Airport for a stress-free departure. Settle any outstanding restaurant reservations or experiences the evening before. Keep one piece of carry-on luggage accessible for any last-minute market purchases.
